provenance: Every case was authored by reading the actual chunk text out of the live collection. No case was derived from filenames, metadata or assumption. Every ground_truth (document_id, chunk_id) pair was verified to resolve to exactly one live point at build time.
jurisdiction_note: The corpus is 100% jurisdiction='Egypt' (1945/1945 points). No jurisdiction-discriminating case is included, because any non-Egypt filter matches zero points and would produce a vacuous case - the defect that made the previous benchmark_cases.json unusable.

confidence_levels.self_verified: Chunk content read directly and unambiguously supports this as the correct answer. Factual or structural; no legal judgment required.
confidence_levels.needs_lawyer: The chunk contains the right facts, but whether it is the legally CORRECT or COMPLETE answer requires a lawyer's sign-off.

cases.query: ما نص المادة 4 من قانون تنظيم التوريدات الحكومية؟

cases.query: ما هو نص المادة 4 نفسها من قانون التوريدات؟
cases.notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-08 after live investigation. The original note claimed the Article 7 and Article 9 chunks (which contain the literal string 'المادة (4)') outrank the real Article 4 chunk. That is FALSE: QueryProcessor.ARTICLE_RE does not match a parenthesised number, so those chunks never carry article_no='4' and never appear in the identifier results at all. The real competition is article 4 of OTHER LAWS - the IP authority law, a WIPO treaty, the constitution - 18 chunks corpus-wide carry article_no='4'. This is a cross-law collision on an unscoped query, not a mention-vs-subject problem. It remains a valid and useful hard case.

cases.query: Article 34 public property
cases.notes: Digit-transposition pair found in the live corpus: Article 34 = Public Property, Article 43 = Suez Canal (chunk_118). Entirely different subjects, so a transposition error is unambiguous. Same class as article 15 vs 51 but a different pair, as required.

cases.query: Article 43 Suez Canal protection
cases.notes: Mirror of adv_article_34_vs_43; guards against a fix that merely biases toward one member of the pair.

cases.query: Article 70 freedom of the press full text
cases.notes: chunk_033 is the table-of-contents entry 'Article 70. Freedom of the press ....... 17' and carries the SAME article_no. The body text (chunk_145) is the answer. Exact identifier matching alone cannot separate these - it needs the semantic half - which makes this a fusion test rather than a lookup test.

cases.query: Article 76 syndicates full text
cases.notes: Second TOC-vs-body instance (TOC is chunk_039), so the behaviour is shown to generalize rather than being one lucky chunk.

cases.query: Article 4 execution period of the agreement
cases.notes: Article 1 (Definitions, chunk_013/chunk_012) is tagged article_no ['1','4'] because it says 'Execution Period means the period specified in Article 4'. The substantive Article 4 text exists only in the ARABIC chunks. Whether the English definitions chunk is an acceptable answer for an English query is a judgment call.  || ADDED 2026-09-08: this case's ground-truth Arabic chunks carry NO article_no at all - their heading is 'المادة (4)' (parenthesised) and their section is 'مدة التنفيذ', so neither extraction path reaches them. The case is therefore only solvable by the semantic half, and it moved 10 -> 12 when identifier ordering changed. Same root cause as the documented OCR/extraction gap; see KNOWN_ISSUES.md.

cases.query: ما هي اجراءات تقييم الاثر البيئي المطلوبة قبل الترخيص للمشروعات الصناعية؟

cases.query: Which clause defines a term commencing 1 February 2026?
cases.notes: Chunk text verbatim: 'Clause 1.3 / 1.3 "Term" means five (5) years commencing 1 February 2026.' A full scan of all 1,945 chunks finds '1 February 2026' in this chunk and no other, so the answer is unique. Exercises the spelled-month date form: M2 extracts '1 February 2026' and normalize_date reduces it to 2026-02-01.

cases.query: ما هي المذكرة الداخلية المؤرخة 15/03/2026؟
cases.notes: Chunk text carries 'التاريخ: 15/03/2026' in the memo header and is the only chunk in the collection containing that date. Exercises the day-first slash form: 15/03/2026 must normalize to 2026-03-15, not 2026-15-03. The corpus settles the day-first-vs-month-first question on its own - it also contains 20/03/2026, which has no month-first reading. Also a near-miss test: the same document carries 12/03/2026 and 20/03/2026 in adjacent chunks, so an implementation that matched on the document rather than the exact date would still look correct at document level and be wrong here.

cases.query: Which payment milestone is due on 2026-05-30?
cases.notes: The date-collision case, and the reason date_ref exists. 2026-05-30 is the phase-1 delivery milestone in the supply contract's payment schedule, and that schedule appears five times across three documents: the Arabic contract (doc_694f11671c02, two chunks), its near-duplicate (doc_7f50f934ecc4) and a standalone payment annex (doc_6786296fd29a, two chunks). All five carry the date verbatim in a table row reading '| Delivery of phase 1 | 30 | 735,000 | 2026-05-30 |', so all five are correct and none can be preferred - exactly the situation article numbers face across statutes.

cases.query: Which provision is dated 24 May 2017?
cases.notes: Both chunks carry '24 May 2017' verbatim: chunk_020 is the promulgation clause ('Article Eight ... Issued at the Presidency of the Republic on 27 Shaban 1438 Hijria / Corresponding to 24 May 2017'), chunk_006 is the standalone heading line of the same phrase. Exercises the abbreviated/spelled-month form alongside a Hijri date the extractor correctly does not match - '27 Shaban 1438' is not picked up, which is right, because normalize_date has no Hijri calendar and inventing one would index a Gregorian key for a Hijri fact.

identifier_date_note: The identifier_date cases were added when ProcessedQuery.identifiers.dates was first wired into retrieval. Ground truth is every chunk carrying the queried date, established by running M2's own extractor over all 1,945 chunks - not by keyword search of the query string. No monetary case exists: QueryProcessor.MONEY_RE matches ASCII ',' only, while the real amounts in this corpus use U+066C ARABIC THOUSANDS SEPARATOR, so every genuine amount extracts truncated. See docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md ISSUE-3. Authoring a monetary case now would mean asserting behaviour that is wrong upstream.
